sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: PISA 2009 targets students aged 15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months who have completed at least six years of formal schooling, regardless of institution type, full-/part-time status, or programme type. The report applies stringent national target population definitions and permissible exclusions; the overall exclusion rate within a country is required to be below 5% to limit distortion of national mean scores. Exclusions can occur at the school level (e.g., remote/inaccessible or very small schools) or at the student level (e.g., intellectual disability or limited proficiency in the language of the test). The excerpt also notes that some indicators use only students with valid information on the ESCS index (e.g., for calculating the percentage below proficiency Level 2).

The assessment design includes pencil-and-paper tasks in reading, mathematics and science (two hours total) and a 30-minute student questionnaire covering background, learning habits, attitudes, and motivation; school principals complete a school questionnaire. The report emphasizes comparability through standardized administration and stringent exclusion rules (overall exclusion rate below 5% within countries). Equity indicators are presented using proficiency benchmarks (e.g., baseline Level 2 in reading), variance decomposition across student, school, and country levels, and socio-economic gradients based on ESCS.
